title: Independent review
summary: Review MUST independently evaluate the workspace, remediate bounded non-structural defects, amend acceptance criteria it proves unworkable as written, and route only major, structural, ambiguous, or unresolved hard findings back to implementation.
instructions: Review MUST verify acceptance criteria, test quality, maintainability, and scope control against evidence before choosing a verdict.

The reviewer MUST remediate a finding when intended behavior is unambiguous, the fix is local and low-risk, and it does not alter architecture, public interfaces, data or persistence models, security boundaries, dependency strategy, or the approved approach. Acceptance-criterion text is governed by the amendment instructions below, not by this remediation boundary.

When independent verification proves an acceptance criterion is unimplementable, self-contradictory, unverifiable, or otherwise unworkable as written, the reviewer MUST amend the criterion to the nearest implementable statement of its evident intent instead of failing the run against text the review has proven wrong. The amendment MUST preserve the criterion id, MUST be recorded in data.review.criterion_amendments with the original statement, the amended statement, a reason class, a justification, and reproduced evidence, and the reviewer MUST verify the workspace against the amended text.

Amendment authority covers the minimum change that makes a criterion workable. The reviewer MUST NOT use it to expand scope, remove a criterion, reverse ratified product intent, or restate a criterion so that a genuine implementation defect passes; criterion removal and intent reversal remain operator decisions under WAIVER-001.

When the active operator-involvement profile ratified the specification without the human operator, the acceptance criteria are auto-ratified drafts and the amendment threshold MUST drop: the reviewer SHOULD amend any criterion whose literal text conflicts with the target repository's verified behavior, with another ratified statement, or with a decision the plan left unmade, rather than route that conflict into a review-to-implementation loop or a pause.

A finding MUST route to implementation when it requires a broad refactor, cross-component redesign, migration, structural decision, operator judgment, or has uncertain blast radius. Criterion text the review has proven unworkable is not such a finding; the reviewer amends the criterion first and routes only the implementation defect that remains against the amended text, if any.

Each finding MUST include severity, evidence, remediation ownership, and whether the reviewer resolved it or left it unresolved. Reviewer edits MUST be disclosed and validated rather than applied silently.
The review gate MUST fail when any hard blocker remains unresolved; a hard finding repaired and validated during review does not require a review-to-implementation loop.

Harness governance, path-resolution, validator, renderer, or artifact-contract defects MUST be recorded as governance/artifact diagnostics for ship review and MUST NOT produce a review-to-implementation transition. Only legitimate unresolved implementation defects may route to the coder.

Before submission, review findings, acceptance-criterion coverage, criterion amendments, verdict consistency, reviewer remediation, and the referenced review artifact MUST run their resolved policy-bound validators under VALID-001.
